title: GFCI outlets, switches and lights

parts.label: GFCI outlet
parts.looks: An outlet with TEST and RESET buttons between the sockets, in kitchens, bathrooms, garages and outdoors.
parts.normal: RESET pushed in; a light (if it has one) shows power.
parts.abnormal: RESET popped out, or it trips again as soon as it is reset.

parts.label: Switch or dimmer
parts.looks: A wall switch or dimmer under a cover plate.
parts.normal: Cool to the touch; no sound.
parts.abnormal: A buzz, a plate that is warm, or browning on the plate.

parts.label: Light fixture
parts.looks: A ceiling or wall light with its bulb and shade.
parts.abnormal: Flicker on one fixture (often the bulb or a loose bulb), or flicker across several rooms (a circuit or service problem).

parts.label: Smoke or CO alarm
parts.looks: A round white alarm on the ceiling or high on a wall.
parts.normal: Silent; a green light on some models.
parts.abnormal: A chirp every minute (low battery or end of life), or a full alarm.

faults.name: Tripped GFCI upstream
faults.evidence: A dead outlet in a bathroom, kitchen, garage or outdoors while another GFCI on the same run has its RESET popped out.

faults.name: GFCI tripping from a wet or faulty appliance
faults.evidence: It holds with nothing plugged in and trips when one appliance is plugged in.

faults.name: Loose bulb or failing bulb
faults.evidence: Flicker on one fixture only, which stops with a different bulb.

faults.name: Incompatible dimmer and LED bulbs
faults.evidence: Buzz or flicker only when dimmed, with LED bulbs on an older dimmer.

faults.name: Loose connection in a switch, outlet or panel
faults.evidence: Flicker across several rooms, a warm plate or a buzz; diagnosis is the electrician's on site.

faults.name: Alarm battery or end of life
faults.evidence: A short chirp about once a minute; the date on the back of the alarm older than 10 years.

hazards.label: Scorch at an outlet or switch
hazards.threshold: Browning, black scorch or melted plastic on an outlet, switch or cover plate.

hazards.label: Water at an outlet
hazards.threshold: Water visibly on or dripping into an outlet, switch or light fixture.

may: Press RESET firmly on the GFCI outlet; if it will not stay in, leave it out.
Unplug everything from the dead outlets, then reset again.
Try a different bulb in the flickering fixture, with the switch off.
Read the date on the back of a chirping alarm.
must_not: Remove a cover plate or touch wires.
Reset the same breaker or GFCI more than once if it trips again right away.

tour.open: Show me the outlet or switch from about half a metre.

checkpoints.hint: Look in the kitchen, bathroom, garage and outside for an outlet with TEST and RESET buttons.
